title: Dance, No One's Watching - Wikipedia
notes: Ezra Collective's third album (Partisan, 27 September 2024), produced by the band. Personnel: Femi Koleoso, drums; TJ Koleoso, bass; Ife Ogunjobi, trumpet; James Mollison, tenor saxophone; Joe Armon-Jones, synthesiser. Ajala recorded in Lagos in October 2023; Expensive's music credited to Fela Kuti; God Gave Me Feet for Dancing with Yazmin Lacey, No One's Watching Me with Olivia Dean.

title: Interview: Ezra Collective's Femi Koleoso on Afrobeat Touch and Hip-Hop Swing (David West, Reverb, 6 August 2020)
notes: Drums in church from four, then Tomorrow's Warriors; took the overnight bus to Paris for lessons with Tony Allen, kit opposite kit ("Why is everything so aggressive? ... you barely have to move"); Max Roach, Art Blakey and Fela; Karriem Riggins, Chris Dave and Clever Austin for hip-hop swing; studio versus live; his Ezra kit a Ludwig Classic Maple with an 18" bass drum, modelled on bebop kits, and a 20" Ludwig Keystone with 12", 16" and 18" toms for Jorja Smith; thick double-ply heads on the jazz kick. title: Streetsnaps: Femi Koleoso (Reggie McCafferty, Hypebeast, 3 November 2022)
notes: In Gorillaz's live band since 2020. Art Blakey and Max Roach lifelong inspirations; Chris Dave and Questlove (for his drum recording methods) among later ones; his all-time favourite is Tony Allen: "Uncle Tony shaped the foundation of the sound I was trying to create."

title: Femi Koleoso - SABIAN Cymbals
notes: Born and lives in London; Ezra Collective and Jorja Smith. Biggest influences: Art Blakey, Tony Allen, Chris Dave. Favourite album he didn't play on: Fela Kuti's Zombie. Favourite SABIAN cymbal: the 8" Chopper.

title: Ezra Collective and Kojey Radical pay tribute to Tony Allen on new single "No Confusion" (Cerys Kenneally, The Line of Best Fit, 1 November 2022)
notes: Koleoso: "Drum lessons with Uncle Tony didn't just change my life, but Ezra Collective's ... 'Confusion' by Fela Kuti is one of the only recorded drum solos by Uncle Tony - it's so him, no one else could have played it."

title: Fifteen Questions Interview with Ezra Collective (15 Questions, November 2022)
notes: "Earliest influence would be Fela Kuti, from my dad's CD collection"; "London, Nigerian, Jubilee Church, Son of an Immigrant"; on Tony Allen's death, "I got all my records out and blasted them"; "Just trying to write hard drum beats."
